title: Grateful Dead Live at Betty Nelson's Organic Raspberry Farm on 1968-09-02
lineage: SBD > Master Reel (Three half-inch four track reels, recorded on Ampex 440) > Master Dat (Sony R500) > SEK'D Prodif Plus > Samplitude v7.02 Professional > Cool Edit Pro v2.0 > SHN

ai_review.summary: Clean soundboard capture of a fiery ’68 set with smoking Dark Star, St. Stephen, The Eleven and Alligator→Caution, though the track‑list is a mess.
ai_review.review: The Miller soundboard from September 2 1968 delivers a vivid, crisp mix that lets the band’s high‑energy improvisations shine – especially the monster Dark Star, tight St. Stephen, soaring The Eleven and the wild Alligator→Caution sequence.  While the recording suffers from occasional vocal level quirks, drum‑heavy balance and duplicated/incorrect track names, the musical performance is consistently strong and worthy of repeated listening.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the show 4‑5 stars and praise the performance; recording quality is generally praised as clean despite some mix glitches, leading to an overall strong rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Super‑clean presence and balance with crisp highs; occasional vocal level issues, drums a bit forward, and several track‑listing errors that cause repeats or missing sections (e.g., cut before Death Don’t Have No Mercy).

show_quality.setlist_flow: Fast‑paced, jam‑heavy ’68 set that builds energy through massive improvisations; despite the chaotic track order on the archive page, the musical flow remains tight and exciting.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Guitar tone described as perfect; flies through extended jams and delivers a powerful solo after the drums.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass work noted for changing rhythm and key during The Eleven, providing a smooth transition.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mix emphasizes drums (sometimes too loud); drum sections are highlighted as strong, especially the post‑Alligator solo.
